column1: # Game profile of Red Dead Redemption (Switch, base game 1.0.1). Plays on the Mac (to the first open-world area: the Ricketts farm), not tried on the iPhone
# Rockstar's RAGE engine as Double Eleven ported it (the engine classes are in the d11 namespace; threads named [RAGE] ... and [RDR2] Render Thread), SDK 15.3.2, on NVN. Modules main and sdk.

# RomFS: 134 RPF6 archives (.rpf; the shaders are in shaders.rpf as rgxd resources, 3,583 of them with those in main and in langselect.pkdswitch) and .bk2 videos. main holds no glslc and no NVNS / BNSH.
# The values below began as scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py's guess (profile_guess.py) and are the ones the game was brought up with. The shader tables are the split's output; see README.md
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB − 1207 MB of bss (counted as used memory): a 2048 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon (Big Brain Academy: Brain vs. Brain sets a heap only then)
# the survey's guess from the RomFS top-level folders: the game's shaders are not in files of those names (rpf resources, main, one .pkdswitch), so these groups label little
# used memory for the current rewritten modules, at least the default 64 MB
